notes:
Summary: Enterprise evaluation focused on reserved GPU pool planning across regions/AZs. Primary ask: predictable throughput + failover headroom for mission-critical grid control agent. Stakeholders: Carlos Mendes (Head ML Infra), Anya Roberts (Director Infra Ops), Tom Briggs (Procurement).

POC ask / technical constraints: 
- Need reserved capacity in 3 regions: us-west (primary), us-east (hot failover), eu-west (data residency + DR).
- Target steady-state throughput: 2.5k concurrent chat sessions (avg 40 tok/sec) => ~100k tok/s sustained; burst headroom for maintenance or traffic spikes = 30% at region level.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 90ms, p99 < 150ms for short-turn chat calls (<=256 tokens). Some longer telemetry summarization calls ok at p99 < 400ms.
- Routing policy requirement: geo-prefixed routing with automatic failover; preference to route to region-local model variant first, fail to compatible quantized variant if capacity constrained.
- Cache/kv requirements: need prefix caching across sessions for operator prompts; must ensure cross-region cache invalidation strategy.

SLA / procurement points raised: 
- Want 99.95% uptime SLA for Dedicated pools with 4-hour RTO for regional failure and credits for partial degradation.
- Request explicit maintenance windows and notice periods; ask for credits if maintenance impacts >3% of monthly tokens.
- Require dedicated support escalation path (phone + pager for Sev1), 30-min response for Sev1.
- Negotiating retained capacity vs burstable shared pool pricing; Procurement pushing for commit + burst buffer pricing banding.

Security / compliance: 
- EU workloads must stay in eu-west region for telemetry PII (discuss data residency proof).
- KMS integration mandatory; customer-managed keys preferred.
- Audit logging retention 1 year min; retention controls for token-level logs.

POC plan + success metrics: 
- 12-week POC: week 0 sizing + config; week 1-3 baseline perf (latency/throughput); week 4-8 soak + failover sim; week 9-12 tuning + runbook handoff.
- Success: meet p95 latency targets at 85% of baseline capacity; automated failover < 2 min with <10% error delta; cost per 1M tokens within vendor estimate +/-15%.
